pick.headline: Colonel Natusch Busch seizes power in Bolivia
pick.summary: On 1 November 1979 Colonel Alberto Natusch Busch overthrew Bolivia's interim civilian president, Walter Guevara Arze, only months after elections.
pick.significance: The coup cut short Bolivia's return to civilian rule and met a general strike and bloody street resistance; Natusch gave way within about two weeks. It was one of a run of Bolivian coups that made the country a byword for instability in Washington's view of the Andes.
pick.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 1 November 1979 opened its Bolivia section with a run of coup items: the military ousting President Guevara, Colonel Natusch named as leader and new president, and a presidency spokeswoman condemning the coup.

alternates.headline: East Germany reopens its border with Czechoslovakia
alternates.summary: On 1 November 1989 East Germany lifted the restrictions it had imposed on travel to Czechoslovakia, reopening the route by which thousands of its citizens were reaching the West through Prague.
alternates.significance: The exodus through Czechoslovakia drained the GDR of young workers and showed that its leadership could no longer hold its population in. Eight days later the Berlin Wall opened.
alternates.fbis: East Berlin's Voice of GDR reported on 1 November that thousands of GDR citizens had travelled to the CSSR that day after the passport and visa suspension was lifted, with more gathering at the West German embassy in Prague.
